intended_object: Coends are functorial: a natural transformation f : F ⟶ G between bifunctors Jᵒᵖ ⥤ J ⥤ C induces a morphism ∫^j F(j,j) ⟶ ∫^j G(j,j) between their coends (here the chosen coends). Its component at j is f_{j,j} followed by the coprojection ι_j. This comes from the docstring and from the later use in `chosenCoendFunctor`.
explanation:
The definition uses the universal property of the chosen coend (`chosenCoend.desc`) applied to the family j ↦ f_{(j,j)} ≫ ι_G(j). This family is a cowedge for F: G's cowedge condition, together with the naturality of f in both variables, gives the required compatibility. So the result is the unique map satisfying ι_F(j) ≫ map f = f_{j,j} ≫ ι_G(j), which is exactly the standard functoriality of coends; the lemmas `ι_map`, `map_id` and `map_comp` confirm this.

The generality is right. J and C are arbitrary categories, and the only assumption is that chosen coends exist (`ChosenCoendsOfShape`). This is the chosen-data counterpart of Mathlib's `coend.map`, which uses `HasCoend` instead, and it is stated in the same generality.
